 Real Betis v Feyenoord Prediction: 8/5 Betis backed to win a thriller
 Partner Authors
 Updated: 8 hours ago
 Real Betis have already seen off European regulars Porto and Lille this season and have enjoyed a phenomenal start to the UEFA Champions League campaign as they prepare to host Feyenoord on Wednesday night. 
 Feyenoord's only defeat this term came away to Barcelona in their first UEFA Champions League tie, and the attack-minded visitors will be looking to make amends on their return to Spain.

 Real Betis v Feyenoord Prediction
 Best Bet: Over 3.5 goals @ 10/11 
 Both of Real Betis’ UEFA Champions League fixtures this season have been 3-2 wins for the Spaniards and, considering how both teams favour attacking football, it would not be a surprise to see a similar scoreline on Wednesday.
 Over 3.5 goals has landed in Los Verdiblancos’ last three competitive games, with these fixtures averaging a massive 6.33 goals per game, and Feyenoord are heading to Seville off the back of a seven-goal thriller at the weekend.
 Four or more goals have been scored in nine of their last 10 matches, including both league phase ties, and another high-scoring affair looks to be on the cards.
 Alternative Bet: Real Betis to win & both teams to score @ 8/5 
 Both of these sides have shipped five goals to Barcelona in recent times but it is Real Betis who are backed to emerge victorious on Wednesday evening.
 The hosts, playing in this competition for the first time since 2005/06, have won six of their last eight in all competitions and their weekend defeat to Barcelona was their first failure to win at home this season.
 They have conceded nine goals in their last three at Estadio de La Cartuja, though, so expect a Feyenoord side that have scored 21 goals in their last five matches to get on the scoresheet.
 Real Betis v Feyenoord Bet Builder Tip
 Cucho Hernandez to score or assist 
 Anis Hadj Moussa to score 
 Antony 4+ shots 
 Nacho Ferri 2+ fouls won 
 Pays 13/1 
 Cucho Hernandez scored off the bench against Porto in Real Betis’ last UEFA Champions League tie and that could earn him a starting berth on Wednesday.
 That was his fifth goal contribution of the season and his fourth in his last six appearances, so the Colombia international will fancy his chances against Feyenoord.
 De Stadionclub have plenty of firepower of their own, though, not least of whom is Anis Hadj Moussa.
 The 24-year-old attacker has scored six goals this season and has found the net six times for club and country in his last six appearances, including against Como in their last outing in this competition.
 Former Manchester United winger Antony is yet to find the net this season, but that is not for lack of trying.
 He has registered an astonishing 42 shots, averaging 5.25 shots per 90 minutes and having at least four attempts on goal in eight of his 10 appearances.
 Nach Ferri appeals in the fouls market for Feyenoord after drawing a club-high 18 fouls in 10 appearances. He has been fouled at least twice in four of his last five games, totalling 15 fouls drawn in this period.
